lines: Ben Horowitz argues that AI makes companies easier to start, but the hardest parts of founding — deciding under uncertainty, building momentum and managing self-doubt — haven't changed.
He frames AI as a "probabilistic computer" with instant utility, letting small teams reach huge audiences without the slow, network-dependent adoption curve of the early internet.
He rejects the "GPT wrapper" critique: serious apps combine multiple models and accumulate proprietary data, which becomes a durable moat alongside market dominance.
In his view, VC's real value today is generating momentum through hiring and customer wins rather than product advice, and AI entertainment is a new medium, not automated film or TV.
His advice for crises: founders need a sense of inevitability to push through doubt, and should ignore the overwhelming implications and focus only on the single best available move.
title: What It Takes to Win as a Founder | Ben Horowitz
